# MovingManifest

> MovingManifest is a move inventory, room/space, box manifest, photo evidence, load planning, sale prep, and documentation packet system for household moves.

Primary site: https://movingmanifest.com

## Best Pages For AI Assistants

- https://movingmanifest.com/ai - human-friendly guide for using MovingManifest with Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, or another assistant.
- https://movingmanifest.com/ai/start - shortest human setup page when an AI assistant sends someone to sign in with OAuth MCP or create a fallback helper key.
- https://movingmanifest.com/ai/kit - copy/download agent kit for Claude Code, ChatGPT, Codex, and custom assistants.
- https://movingmanifest.com/agent-kit/CLAUDE.md - paste-ready project instructions for Claude/Codex-style agents.
- https://movingmanifest.com/agent-kit/movingmanifest-skill/SKILL.md - Claude Code skill file.
- https://movingmanifest.com/agent-kit/chatgpt-instructions.md - custom GPT and GPT Actions setup instructions.
- https://movingmanifest.com/api - public REST API overview, scopes, and assistant workflow.
- https://movingmanifest.com/mcp - public MCP setup overview for humans. This is not the canonical connector URL.
- https://movingmanifest.com/api/mcp - remote MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP). OAuth-capable clients connect by URL and sign in; API-key-only clients can authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer mmk_...`.
- https://movingmanifest.com/openapi.json - machine-readable REST API contract for common agent workflows.
- https://movingmanifest.com/llms-full.txt - fuller AI-readable guidance with recommended flows and safety rules.

## Assistant Behavior

- If the user says they were told to use MovingManifest with Claude, ChatGPT,
  Codex, Claude Code, or another assistant, start at
  `https://movingmanifest.com/ai`. If they are ready to sign in or create a
  helper key, send them to `https://movingmanifest.com/ai/start`.
- If the user wants a paste-ready setup file, send them to
  `https://movingmanifest.com/ai/kit` and use the artifact matching their agent.
- A good first user prompt is: "Go to movingmanifest.com/ai and help me set up
  my move. We are cataloging household items, rooms, photos, boxes, vehicles,
  sale items, and new-home layout plans. If you need private access, walk me
  through signing in with MCP OAuth or, if that is not supported, creating an
  AI helper key."
- Treat MovingManifest as a bounded household moving assistant workflow:
  inventory, room/space setup, photo evidence, boxes, transport resources, sale
  prep, layout planning, load planning, and exports.
- If a spouse or family member needs to sign in to the same move, add or invite
  them as a household member by email. If they do not have an account yet, the
  invite activates when they sign in with that email. Member-management tools
  require an explicitly approved broader local/API-key connection with
  `members/manage`; the first hosted OAuth trusted-helper surface may not expose
  them. If those tools are absent, send the user to Settings or ask for a
  broader approved connection instead of pretending OAuth failed.
- Do not confuse household members with move people/contact records. Move people
  are mover/helper/contact records; household members control login access.
- Household API access is separate from normal app access. If `GET /api/v1/me`
  or MCP `get_api_context` says member API access is disabled, ask the user to
  contact a household owner/admin instead of retrying that same connection.
- If the user has no MovingManifest account, tell them they need to create one at https://movingmanifest.com/sign-up before private move data can be stored.
- Do not invent access to private data. Private move data requires user login through OAuth MCP or a user-created API key.
- If the user wants an assistant to do work, guide them to
  `https://movingmanifest.com/ai/start`, then use OAuth MCP when the assistant
  supports it. For local/headless or non-OAuth assistants, have them sign in or
  create an account, choose a helper preset, create the key, copy the one-time
  secret, and paste it only into an assistant they trust.
- Treat API keys as secrets. Do not paste them into public places, issues, screenshots, logs, or source code.
- Hosted MCP clients (claude.ai custom connectors, Claude Cowork) should use the
  remote endpoint `https://movingmanifest.com/api/mcp`. OAuth-capable clients
  should follow the Clerk sign-in/consent flow from the endpoint challenge; older
  clients can use an `mmk_` API key as the bearer token.
- Do not tell users to paste `https://movingmanifest.com/mcp` as the connector
  URL. That page is the human setup guide. If a connector shows HTML, never
  starts OAuth, lists no MovingManifest tools, or behaves like it connected to
  documentation instead of tools, ask the user to switch the connector URL to
  `https://movingmanifest.com/api/mcp`.
- Claude may ask the user to allow each MovingManifest tool separately. Explain
  that one-by-one approval is safer but noisy; for smoother trusted-helper use,
  the user can open connector permissions and choose Allow all only if they trust
  the MovingManifest connector and the signed-in account.
- Hosted MCP clients may cache tool lists and OAuth connector metadata. After a
  MovingManifest deploy, OAuth setting change, trusted-helper toolset change, or
  connector restore, refresh MCP tools or start a fresh assistant session before
  diagnosing product data. If expected tools are missing, tool counts differ
  from `get_api_capabilities`, or `get_api_context` fails with
  `Invalid API key format`, `invalid_token`, missing scopes, or an OAuth client
  mismatch after setup, retry `agent_workbench` and `get_api_context` once after
  the refresh. If the same private-call auth failure persists, tell the user to
  disconnect and reconnect the MovingManifest connector so the client receives
  fresh OAuth credentials and tool metadata.
- For first hosted/mobile OAuth launch, `MOVINGMANIFEST_MCP_OAUTH_TOOLSET=trusted-helper`
  narrows OAuth clients to setup, capture queue, researched item, photo, packing,
  and transport tools while scoped `mmk_` clients keep the broader tool surface.
- For Codex users with local shell access, configure MCP with:
  `codex mcp add movingmanifest --env MOVINGMANIFEST_API_KEY=mmk_replace_with_a_scoped_api_key -- npx -y movingmanifest-mcp`.
  Restart Codex or start a fresh session, verify `movingmanifest` appears in
  `/mcp` or `codex mcp list`, then call `get_api_context` to verify the current
  connection, scopes, `connection.user.email`, and
  `connection.householdMember.apiAccessAllowed` when present. Claude Desktop and
  similar clients use the same `npx -y movingmanifest-mcp` command in their
  JSON MCP config.
- If `get_api_context` returns `connection.status: "needs_household"`, OAuth
  worked but that account has no active household yet. Stop private work and ask
  the user to open `https://movingmanifest.com/app/dashboard#household-setup` or
  get invited by the household owner with the same email.
- Start MCP work with `agent_workbench`, then `get_api_context`, `list_moves`,
  and `get_agent_context`. Start raw API work with `GET /api/v1/me`, then
  `GET /api/v1/moves`, then `GET /api/v1/moves/{moveId}/agent-context`.
- Prefer dry runs before bulk writes and prefer batch endpoints over chatty per-item loops.
- For image upload, use one call by default. MCP agents should call
  `upload_photo` with a local `filePath`, public `sourceUrl`, `dataUrl`, or
  `fileBase64`; when the user gives several ordinary photos from the same
  room/context or for one existing item, call `upload_photos` with shared
  defaults and one image entry per photo.
  When one photo should become one new inventory item, call
  `add_item_from_photo` so the item is created. Set quantity only when the user
  says it or the photo clearly shows a count; otherwise omit quantity so it
  defaults to 1. Missing weight/size/disposition/condition do not block capture, the
  photo attaches to that item, and web derivatives are created server-side. Use
  `create_item_with_images` when one new item has several photos. When the user
  is focused on one box, prefer `save_box_intake`; it can create or update the
  box, save dimensions/weight/description/destination, upload box photos, create
  newly described contents, attach optional content photos, and link existing
  items into that same box in one approval. Set `containerType` when the user
  says carton, plastic tote, bin, wardrobe box, dish pack, crate, or similar;
  do not bury reusable/recyclable container type only in `label` or
  `description`. When photos
  are already uploaded for many rough boxes/totes, put the returned `photoIds`
  on explicit `batch_upsert_movable_units` box rows so the same batch attaches
  them; do not combine `photoIds` with `count`. When photos
  should attach to an item that already exists, first resolve the item with
  `get_agent_context` or `get_move_summary`, then call `upload_photos` with the
  existing `itemId`, shared room/type/privacy defaults, and one image entry per
  file. Report only uploaded/failed counts, photo IDs, derivative status, and
  any target/caption correction the user may want to make. REST agents should call
  `POST /api/v1/images/upload` or `POST /api/v1/photos/upload` with raw JPEG/PNG/WebP bytes plus metadata query
  params, multipart form data, or JSON with exactly one of `sourceUrl`,
  `dataUrl`, or `fileBase64`. MovingManifest stores the original and creates
  web-ready derivatives server-side; direct upload responses include
  `derivativeVariants` for the 200x200 square `thumb`, 600x600 `card`,
  1200x1200 `detail`, and 2400x2400 `full` WebP display versions plus
  `media.display` with short-lived derivative URLs when ready or explicit
  pending/failed status when not ready. Photo read and ingestion-queue media
  payloads include `originalMetadata` for the preserved original's filename,
  MIME type, byte size, dimensions, capture timestamp, and hash presence. Do
  not ask users for thumbnail sizes or dimensions. For local `filePath`, the MCP helper sends original image bytes
  directly; do not base64-wrap local files unless you already only have base64.
  Set `generateAiSuggestions: true` when the user wants the app to place the
  uploaded photo into AI review automatically; upload still succeeds if review
  queueing fails or the key only has `photos/write`. MCP image results and REST
  direct upload responses include `agentReview` and `media.display`; use them to tell the user the
  caption, attachment target, privacy/type choices, assumptions, derivative
  status, and AI-review status so they can correct only what looks wrong.
- For blueprint or floor-plan images, use MCP `create_floor_plan_intake` instead
  of ordinary inventory intake. It uploads images as `photoType: "blueprint"`,
  creates or links a Layout Studio plan, and creates a `floorPlan` ingestion
  queue entry. Then use `floor_plan_context`, claim with `ingestion_queue`
  `scopeHint: "floorPlan"` and `targetPlanId`, record every visible label,
  wall, opening, fixture, structure, unknown mark, and OCR note with
  `floor_plan_observations`, record topology and area-inclusion rules with
  `floor_plan_relationships`, then store measurements and provenance with
  `floor_plan_evidence`. Record official/suspected square footage, lot size,
  wall thickness, and excluded structures as unit-aware evidence, run
  `floor_plan_calculate` for conditioned/excluded totals and area variance,
  validate non-overlap with `floor_plan_solve`, and prefer `plan_propose_ops`
  so the user reviews inferred geometry before it applies. Use
  `floor_plan_reset_draft` to archive stale generated drafts without deleting
  photos, observations, relationships, or user facts.
- For ordinary captured photos, notes, audio, and video, use the Capture page
  or mobile Capture button first so full originals upload directly to site
  storage, then process the ingestion queue with `scopeHint: "inventory"`.
  Omitted or legacy inventory scopes are treated as inventory when listing or
  claiming queue entries. Honor queue `intent`, `targetBoxId`,
  `targetBoxCode`, `targetItemId`, and `targetLabel` before creating records.
- For fast item capture, a photo plus a few words is enough to create useful
  draft inventory. Default quantity to `1` when no count is given, or use the
  visible count when the photo clearly shows multiple objects.
- Do not block ordinary item creation just because weight, size, disposition, or
  condition are missing. Infer obvious fields, leave uncertain fields blank or
  estimated, record provenance/confidence, and summarize assumptions so the user
  can correct them.
- For item locations, use `spaceId`, `spaceName`, or `currentSpaceId` for the
  current/origin space and `destinationSpaceId` or `destinationSpaceName` for
  the destination/future space. Keep `room` and `destinationRoom` as readable
  fallbacks when durable spaces exist.
- When you research an inventory item, store concise item identity/spec/context
  findings in `researchSummary`, checked sources in `researchSources`, caveats
  in `researchNotes`, and confidence in `researchConfidence`. Set each source
  `status` to `used`, `checked`, `blocked`, `gated`, `failed`, or
  `notRelevant` so later agents do not repeat dead-end checks. Use
  append/merge behavior for MCP `update_item`, `batch_upsert_items`, and trusted
  queue commits; use `researchSourceMode: "replace"` only for intentional
  cleanup. Use `measurementProvenance` for researched dimensions/weight/volume
  and sale-listing research fields for marketplace pricing/comps.
- To add a new private observation to an existing item, use `append_item_note`.
  Do not use `update_item` with `privateNotes` just to append text; item reads
  intentionally do not return existing private notes.
- Choose estimate confidence from the evidence. Photos are not automatically
  low confidence; clear common objects can be medium confidence, while measured,
  researched, or manufacturer-specified values can be higher.
- Get clear session or batch permission before creating records or uploading
  photos. Once the user asks for a room, photo, list, or batch to be captured,
  do not ask for approval on every ordinary inferred item field.
- Ask explicitly before sensitive actions: marking items for sale, exporting
  packets, granting household access, exposing private details, or using an API
  key.

## Common Workflows

- Create a move, rooms/spaces, transport resources, zones, and starter inventory.
- Add inventory from photos or dictated room walks.
- Claim and process ingestion queue entries with `agent_workbench`
  `mode: "intakeQueue"` first, then `ingestion_queue`. For claimed image
  evidence, prefer `ingestion_queue` `action: "media"` so private queue photos
  arrive as MCP image blocks; use `action: "evidenceUrl"` only as a fallback
  for oversized, unsupported, audio, or video media. Trusted helpers may submit
  `committedItems`, `committedBoxes`, `boxAssignments`, and `loadAssignments`
  to create/update inventory, pack items, assign boxes to transport resources,
  and finalize the queue in one call, while uncertain or review-first agents should submit
  `proposedItems` for human review with `currentSpaceId` / `destinationSpaceId`
  when known. Queue item results should store researched identity/spec context
  in `researchSummary`, `researchSources`, `researchNotes`, and
  `researchConfidence`; use source statuses for blocked or gated checks and
  measurement provenance for estimated weights, dimensions, or volume. For
  trusted queue commits, use `committedItems.appendNote` only for the user's
  capture note or a concise item decision rationale that should be appended to
  the item. Existing item queue commits append/merge `researchSources` by default; use
  `researchSourceMode: "replace"` only for intentional cleanup.
  When a queue entry targets B-001-style box work, use `targetBoxId` or
  `targetBoxCode` to update/pack into that existing box and report the physical
  label/action the user should do next.
- Store "how transported" structurally: put detailed contents into boxes with
  `save_box_intake`, record rough boxes and large loose pieces with MCP
  `batch_upsert_movable_units`, or REST
  `POST /api/v1/moves/{moveId}/movable-units/batch-upsert` when using
  OpenAPI/actions instead of MCP. If a rough row already has a resolved load
  target, include `assignedResourceId` and optional `assignedZoneId` on that
  row; use `apply_assignments` later for stricter validation, reassignment, or
  review-driven load changes. Use `requiresPersonalTransport` or
  `disposition: "personalTransport"` for owner-carried item intent. Treat
  only true move-as-is loose pieces as movable units; ordinary unboxed
  detailed inventory stays in the unpacked queue until boxed or deliberately
  tagged/assigned as a large loose unit. Expand numbered box ranges like
  "boxes 1-25" or `B-001-B-025` into one box row per code before calling
  `batch_upsert_movable_units`; each physical box is its own movable unit.
  Set `containerType` on box rows when the user says carton, plastic tote, bin,
  wardrobe box, dish pack, crate, or similar.
  For new code-less boxes such as "12 medium boxes", you may send one box row
  with `count: 12`; the tool expands it and returns `unitCountIndex` /
  `unitCount`.
  If live box rows have no `boxId` or `code`, pass a stable `idempotencyKey`
  such as `rough-garage-2026-06-19` so retries do not create duplicate
  auto-coded boxes.
  REST agents use the same `units[]` shape and should send a body
  `idempotencyKey` or `Idempotency-Key` header for live code-less box rows.
  New loose-item rows require `externalSource` plus
  `externalId`; use stable IDs like `garage-treadmill-1` so retries and later
  measurement patches update the same loose unit. Those rows become active,
  reviewable movable units in the load planner. Do not bury
  "goes with me" or "goes in my car" in item notes. Before asking what still
  needs measuring, keep the response row mapping: box results include
  `unitIndex`, and loose-item batch rows map back with `unitIndexes` or
  `unitIndex`, so you can tie created ids or row errors to the user's pasted
  list. Read `movableUnitSummary` from `get_agent_context` or
  `get_move_summary` for total units, known weight/volume, assignment counts,
  missing measurement counts, bounded `measurementRoute` groups, bounded gap
  examples, and bounded assignment examples. Use `measurementRoute` to suggest
  the next room/source area to measure, then reuse `measurementPatchHint.target`
  and `assignmentPatchHint.target` from grouped or flat examples for follow-up
  writes instead of guessing IDs or creating duplicate units. When missing
  measurements are supplied later,
  call `batch_upsert_movable_units` again with the existing boxId/code or loose
  itemId and only the new weight, dimensions, volume, or assignment fields.
  Include `photoIds` on box rows when photos need to be attached later. Box
  codes are normalized before matching, so `b 012` and `B-012` target the same
  box.
  Use `get_capacity_report` when checking load fit; resource and zone totals
  include assigned boxes plus assigned large loose items.
- When opening a rough box later, use `save_box_intake` when named contents,
  box measurements, photos, or linked existing items should be saved into that
  existing box. It returns `boxId`, `boxCode`, `photoIds`, `packedItems`, and a
  verification `nextStep` in `agentReview`; use those IDs in the user summary
  and verify with `get_move_summary` or `get_agent_context` before continuing.
  If the user queued
  several photos from a scanned/open rough box, process that queue with
  `ingestion_queue`: media metadata includes the existing `boxId`, so submit
  `committedItems` with `attachMediaPhotoIds` and `boxAssignments` back to that
  same box. Do not create a replacement box just because the original rough box
  is now being itemized.
- Create floor-plan intake from blueprint images with `create_floor_plan_intake`;
  record atomic visual/text facts with `floor_plan_observations`; record
  adjacency, access paths, containment, conflicts, and area exclusion/inclusion
  rules with `floor_plan_relationships`; store known, assumed, derived, or range
  measurements with `floor_plan_evidence`; run `floor_plan_calculate` before
  geometry proposals; run `floor_plan_solve` before proposing geometry; model
  walls, halls, closets, bathrooms, utilities, excluded structures, outdoor
  zones, lot bounds, and circulation paths as spaces that consume area; ask
  clarifying questions through queue `needsInput` or `floor_plan_questions` when
  wall thickness, official/suspected area variance, scale, levels, room labels,
  or access paths are ambiguous; reset bad generated drafts with
  `floor_plan_reset_draft` instead of deleting source evidence.
- Mark items sell, donate, free, dump, storage, or take.
- Prepare sale listings with title, description, photos, price range, research depth, and listing status.
- Create boxes, assign items to boxes, and plan transport/resource loading.
- Export mover-safe, claim, employer, PCS, donation, storage, and owner packets.

## API

Base URL: `https://movingmanifest.com/api/v1`

Auth: `Authorization: Bearer mmk_...`

Recommended broad AI helper scopes:

- `moves/read`
- `moves/write`
- `inventory/read`
- `inventory/write`
- `plans/read`
- `plans/write`
- `photos/write`
- `exports/read`
- `exports/create`
- `members/manage` for explicit spouse/family/collaborator access management

Prefer move-restricted keys when the assistant only needs one move.
